item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 121710
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Mon Oct 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, centered about 60 miles off the coast of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP93):
A broad area of low pressure located several hundred miles
south-southwest of the coast of Guatemala continues to produce
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. This system is gradually
becoming better defined, and environmental conditions are forecast
to be conducive for further development. A tropical depression is
expected to form well south of southern Mexico in the next two days
while the system moves generally west-northwestward at around 10
mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 21a
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 121737
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Intermediate Advisory Number 21A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
1100 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
...SIMON DRIFTING WESTWARD AS A CATEGORY 2 HURRICANE...
...DANGEROUS WINDS EXPECTED FOR A FEW MORE HOURS WITH FLOODING RAINS
TO CONTINUE ALONG THE COAST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM MST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.2N 106.6W
ABOUT 60 MI...95 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 210 MI...335 KM S OF MAZATLAN MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...105 MPH...165 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...965 MB...28.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None. 
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* North of Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya
 
A Tropical Storm Warning in in effect for...
* Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area within 48 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case for the
next few hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in west-central Mexico should continue to
monitor as changes to watches and warnings are possible later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM MST (1800 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 20.2 North, longitude 106.6 West. Simon is drifting 
toward the west near 2 mph (4 km/h), but is forecast to resume a 
slow northwestward motion by tonight which should then continue 
into early Tuesday. A gradual turn toward the northeast is forecast 
thereafter, and Simon is expected to approach the west-central 
Mexico coastline on Wednesday into Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 105 mph (165 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Some additional weakening is forecast today, but 
Simon could re-intensify some on Tuesday and Wednesday and is 
expected to remain a hurricane through midweek. Rapid weakening is 
likely after Simon moves inland late this week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60
miles (95 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 965 mb (28.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are likely to occur in the Hurricane 
Warning area of Las Islas Marias beginning tonight into Tuesday. 
Tropical storm conditions are expected to occur for a few more hours 
in the Tropical Storm warning area. Hurricane conditions are 
possible within the watch area by Wednesday, with tropical storm 
conditions possible by Tuesday night.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of
2 to 4 inches across coastal portions of southwest and west-central
Mexico with isolated additional amounts of 6 to 8 inches over
portions of the state of Jalisco through early this week, and the
state of Sinaloa mainly Wednesday and Thursday. Isolated maximum
storm totals of 30 inches are possible over portions of the states
of Michoacan, Colima, and Jalisco.  This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides or worsen any on-going
flooding, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is likely along the immediate 
coast near Las Islas Marias. Near the coast, the surge will be 
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
821 
WTPZ45 KNHC 121459
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
Simon's interaction with the coast of Mexico has made it a very 
compact hurricane. The satellite presentation this morning consists 
of a very small central dense overcast with a warm spot in the 
center which still appears to be a small eye. The convection is also 
very electrically active, with substantial lightning occurring in 
the eastern eyewall. A 1110 UTC GPM microwave pass showed that 
Simon's inner core remains intact, though with the eye open on the 
northwest side. This structure is consistent with some mid-level 
easterly shear that appears to be undercutting the outflow layer, 
looking at some area-average soundings from the HAFS-A/B 
initialization this morning. Satellite intensity estimates have a 
large range this morning, as low as CI 4.1/67 kt from the UW-CIMSS 
ADT, or as high as CI 5.5/102 kt from the latest subjective Dvorak 
fix. The initial intensity is lowered slightly to 95 kt for this 
advisory, favoring a blend of the latest SATCON (100 kt) and D-MINT 
(85-90 kt) estimates.
 
Based on satellite images, Simon continues to move very slowly to 
the northwest, with an estimated motion of 315 degrees at 3 kt. This 
very slow motion is the result of competing steering influences from 
a distant mid-level ridge centered over the Texas Gulf coast, and 
another weaker mid-level ridge placed southwest of Simon over the 
eastern Pacific. In general the steering imparted by the ridge to 
the northwest should be a little stronger, and thus Simon is 
expected to maintain a very slow northwestward motion over the next 
24-36 h. After that period, a large trough with an embedded 
short-wave is expected to amplify and move into the southwestern 
United States, and this trough is expected to extend far enough 
southward to impart a little more westerly flow that should 
ultimately turn Simon to the north-northeast in the 48-72 hour time 
frame. With that said, the track guidance is not at all in agreement 
on how quickly this turn will occur. The latest 06 UTC GFS and 
HAFS-A/B runs almost immediately move Simon northward and then 
north-northeast, resulting in a much faster landfall back in 
mainland Mexico. By contrast, the 06 UTC ECMWF run shows a 
short-term westward track that meanders offshore to the southeast of 
the Baja California Peninsula before it turns northward and moves up 
into the Gulf of California. The ensemble guidance is also all over 
the place, resembling a squashed spider with substantial spread from 
the southwest to northeast direction. The latest NHC track forecast 
has been shifted westward and is quite a bit slower, following the 
latest trends in the track guidance. However, this track is not 
nearly as slow or as far west as the latest Google DeepMind ensemble 
mean (GDMI) or its newer Weather Next Model (WN3I). Given the large 
spread in solutions, this remains a low confidence track forecast.
 
Based on the earlier microwave images, Simon still appears to have a
small inner core, and that is an important consideration to take
into account in the forecast over the next few days. While the
hurricane appears to be currently dealing with some mid-level
easterly shear and that may result in a little more short-term
weakening, this shear is expected to subside over the next 24 h as
Simon traverses very warm 30-31 C sea-surface temperatures. In fact,
the latest HMON and HAFS-A/B runs show the small core of Simon
recovering and re-intensifying back into a major hurricane later
this week. Thus, the latest NHC intensity forecast starts to show
some restrengthening after 24 h. Small storms like Simon can also
be prone to rapid changes in intensity, both up or down, which
makes the intensity forecast also more uncertain than usual. This
forecast is initially close to the middle of the guidance but ends
up on the higher side after 48 h. Rapid weakening is still
anticipated when Simon eventually makes landfall later this week
towards the end of the forecast.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Tropical Storm winds are still likely along a portion of the
west-central coast of Mexico for a few more hours, where a Tropical
Storm Warning is in effect.
 
2. Simon is expected to approach the coast of western Mexico later
this week, where hurricane conditions are possible. A Hurricane
Watch is in effect from Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern and west-central Mexico over the next few days. This
rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will affect portions of the southwestern and
west-central coasts of Mexico over the next few days. These swells
are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  12/1500Z 20.1N 106.5W   95 KT 110 MPH
 12H  13/0000Z 20.4N 106.8W   85 KT 100 MPH
 24H  13/1200Z 20.9N 107.3W   80 KT  90 MPH

 96H  16/1200Z 24.1N 106.3W   45 KT  50 MPH...INLAND
120H  17/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Papin
